description: A four-panel, single-style schematic (a)-(d) illustrating how the grain and precipitate structure of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe rolled steel evolves with increasing Be content; orange arrows between the panels mark the direction of increasing Be. Every panel depicts the same cluster of four light-blue hexagonal grains labelled gamma (γ), each crossed by thin yellow-green lines annotated "Annealing twin". (a) 0Be: four γ grains with annealing twins only, no precipitates. (b) 0.5Be: the γ grains and annealing twins are retained and small orange rounded particles labelled "Precipitated phase" appear dispersed inside the grains and along grain boundaries. (c) 1.0Be: the orange precipitates persist and green elongated ellipses labelled α appear inside the γ grains, marking the onset of a γ + α dual-phase structure. (d) 1.5Be: the green α regions become larger, more numerous and variously shaped (elongated and rounded), the green α islands enclose orange precipitates, and the γ matrix carries a denser dispersion of "Precipitated phase". No axes, scale bars or numeric values are present; all labels are text annotations. The figure argues that progressive Be addition stabilises and coarsens α-ferrite inside the γ matrix while continuously increasing the density of precipitated phase.

observations.observation: All four panels show the same motif: four light-blue hexagonal grains labelled γ (austenite) meeting at a triple junction.
Thin yellow-green lines crossing the γ grains are labelled 'Annealing twin' in every panel (a)-(d).
Panel (a) contains only γ grains and annealing twins; no precipitate particles and no α phase are drawn for the 0Be condition.
Small orange rounded particles labelled 'Precipitated phase' first appear in panel (b), the 0.5Be condition.
Green elongated elliptical regions labelled α first appear in panel (c), the 1.0Be condition, indicating a γ + α dual-phase structure.
In panel (d), 1.5Be, the green α regions are larger and more numerous than in (c) and some enclose orange precipitate particles.
Orange arrows drawn between consecutive panels indicate the sequence of increasing Be content from (a) to (d).
The label 'Precipitated phase' appears in panels (b), (c) and (d) but not in (a).
The caption states the panels correspond to rolling-state Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe with (a) 0Be, (b) 0.5Be, (c) 1.0Be and (d) 1.5Be.
The caption states the figure is a schematic diagram of grain and precipitate changes with increasing Be content.
The schematic supports the interpretation that Be addition converts the single-austenite structure into a γ + α dual-phase structure with increasing precipitate density.
No axes, scale bars, colour bars or printed numeric values appear anywhere in the figure; all information is conveyed by symbols and text annotations.

subfigures.description: Schematic of four light-blue hexagonal γ grains joined at a triple junction, each crossed by thin yellow-green lines pointed to by the label 'Annealing twin'. No second phase or precipitates are drawn. Corresponds to 0Be.

Same four γ grains with annealing twins, now containing numerous small orange rounded dots, one of which is pointed to by the label 'Precipitated phase'; grains show slightly irregular boundaries. Corresponds to 0.5Be.

γ grains with annealing twins plus orange 'Precipitated phase' dots, and additionally three green elongated elliptical islands labelled α located inside the γ grains (dual-phase γ + α). Corresponds to 1.0Be.

γ grains with annealing twins and dense orange 'Precipitated phase'; the green α islands are larger and more abundant, of both elongated and rounded shapes, and some green α regions enclose orange precipitates. Corresponds to 1.5Be.
